_about: Closest real proposal in Congress to each CBO option and ready-made plan. Each bill was confirmed through search results quoting congress.gov or govinfo records, sponsors' offices, CRS, CRFB, legiscan or news; congress.gov URLs follow its canonical pattern for the confirmed bill number. Researched November 2026.

income-tax-rates-1pt.note: No bill we found raises every income tax rate by a point.

corp-rate-1pt.title: Corporate Tax Dodging Prevention Act
corp-rate-1pt.match: Goes further: raises the corporate rate from 21% back to 35%.

ss-tax-earnings-over-250k.title: Social Security Expansion Act
ss-tax-earnings-over-250k.match: Applies the payroll tax above $250,000, as here, and also raises benefits.

carbon-tax-25.title: MARKET CHOICE Act
carbon-tax-25.match: Bipartisan carbon tax starting higher, at about $40 a ton, and repealing the gas tax.

vat-5pct.title: Progressive Consumption Tax Act of 2020
vat-5pct.match: A 10% consumption tax, used to cut income taxes rather than the deficit.

cap-health-exclusion.title: Fair Care Act of 2026
cap-health-exclusion.match: Caps the tax break at $10,200 for single and $27,500 for family coverage, within a larger health bill.

limit-itemized-15pct.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (now law)
limit-itemized-15pct.match: Enacted a much milder version: deductions save top-bracket filers at most 35 cents per dollar.

gas-tax-15c.title: Rebuild America Act of 2019
gas-tax-15c.match: Raises fuel taxes 25 cents over five years, then ties them to inflation.

alcohol-tax.title: Alcohol Tax Equalization Act of 2003
alcohol-tax.match: Taxes beer and wine at the liquor rate per unit of alcohol, as here. No newer bill found.

carried-interest.title: Carried Interest Fairness Act of 2025
carried-interest.match: Taxes carried interest as ordinary income, the same policy.

medicare-advantage-benchmarks.title: No UPCODE Act
medicare-advantage-benchmarks.match: Bipartisan; cuts overpayments to private plans by tightening how diagnoses are coded, rather than lowering benchmarks.

site-neutral-hospital-outpatient.title: Preventing Hospital Overbilling of Medicare Act
site-neutral-hospital-outpatient.match: Pays off-campus hospital clinics the same rate as doctors' offices; narrower than this option.

part-b-premium-35pct.note: No bill we found raises Part B premiums this way.

medicaid-per-enrollee-caps.title: American Health Care Act of 2017
medicaid-per-enrollee-caps.match: Capped federal Medicaid funding per enrollee; passed the House 217–213, not the Senate.

raise-full-retirement-age-70.title: Social Security Reform Act of 2016
raise-full-retirement-age-70.match: Raises the full retirement age gradually to 69, not 70.

chained-cpi.title: Social Security Reform Act of 2016
chained-cpi.match: Switches cost-of-living raises to the chained CPI, within a larger Social Security bill.

ss-benefits-high-earners.title: Social Security Reform Act of 2016
ss-benefits-high-earners.match: A more progressive benefit formula that slows benefit growth for higher earners.

cut-defense-budget.title: People Over Pentagon Act of 2023
cut-defense-budget.match: Cuts the Defense Department's budget by $100 billion a year.

cut-transport-education-grants.note: No bill we found cuts both transportation and education grants this way.

crop-insurance-subsidies.title: AFFIRM Act of 2026
crop-insurance-subsidies.match: Caps premium subsidies at $40,000 a farmer and ends them above $250,000 of income.

extend-aca-credits.note: The House passed a three-year extension on January 8, 2026 (230 to 196). The Senate has not voted on it.

extend-obbba-temp-tax.note: No single bill we found makes all ten provisions permanent.

economists.name: The Moment of Truth (the Simpson–Bowles plan)
economists.by: National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform, whose members included sitting senators and representatives
economists.match: A bipartisan mix of spending cuts, tax reform and Social Security changes. It fell short of the votes needed to go to Congress.

revenue.name: The People's Budget, FY2019 (summary by CRFB)
revenue.match: Cut deficits mostly with taxes on high earners and corporations and a carbon tax, while expanding benefits.

spending.name: Fiscal Sanity to Save America (FY2025 budget)
spending.match: Balanced the budget mainly with spending cuts, including a later Social Security retirement age and Medicare changes.

protect.name: Medicare and Social Security Fair Share Act (S. 1690)
protect.by: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Rep. Brendan Boyle (D-PA)
protect.match: A partial match: protects both programs' benefits with taxes on incomes above $400,000, without other savings.
